title: Participatory Development and Tailoring of a Juvenile Risk-Needs Assessment: A Structured Approach to Contextualized Implementation
abstract: Juvenile risk and needs assessment (JRNA) tools are widely used in juvenile justice, but many are developed outside the jurisdictions in which they are implemented. When assessment tools are insufficiently aligned with local legal frameworks, practitioner workflows, and service environments, implementation may be undermined by inconsistent use, limited practitioner trust, and poor organizational fit. This paper describes the structured, multi-phase tailoring of the Nebraska Screening and Assessment Tool, a JRNA developed for diversion settings. Rather than focusing on initial construction and validation, which are reported elsewhere, the study examines a participatory process for tailoring the instrument to routine practice while preserving its empirical structure. Development included practitioner engagement, implementation team review, pilot testing, training, and digital platform development. Refinements addressed item phrasing, response formats, domain sequencing, interview structure, scoring procedures, administration guidance, and platform functionality. The study offers a methodological example of participatory JRNA tailoring within local implementation constraints.
